plan_a_advantages: Includes dedicated threshold and hill training for speed development.
Features a longer long run to build overall endurance.
Incorporates a strength and mobility session to improve stability and injury resistance.
plan_b_advantages: Provides a more consistent recovery schedule.
Offers longer, continuous easy runs which could be beneficial for maintaining volume.
The longer easy runs provide a good base for the other sessions.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more structured approach to building aerobic fitness and strength specific to trail running. While Plan B focuses heavily on recovery and relatively short, easy runs, Plan A includes dedicated threshold work, hill sessions, and a longer long run – all crucial components for improving speed and endurance on technical terrain. The inclusion of a strength and mobility session is also a significant advantage, addressing a common weakness in trail runners. Plan B’s emphasis on recovery, while important, risks hindering progress towards the athlete’s primary goal of increased speed.
